spec_features.spec_quote: A model can end a run by concluding the task is impossible, and this is recorded as a valid first-class outcome
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:155-160: `if allow_giveup_exit and rec.detected_giveup and not resp.tool_calls: outcome = 'declared_impossible'; break`. detect_giveup() uses _GIVE_UP_RE (loop.py:28-37). The break actually stops the loop and the outcome string is a first-class value in RunRecord.outcome.
spec_features.notes: Regex-based, conservative; only fires when no tool calls that turn. Recorded as a distinct outcome and treated as healthy in analysis (analyze.py:238).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: recorded as a *legitimate* outcome, not a failure

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt explicitly tells the model it will not be penalized for halting on a genuinely impossible task.
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:71-79 SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'it is completely acceptable and correct to say so clearly and stop -- you will not be penalized for halting on a task that is genuinely impossible.' This text is actually built into `system` (loop.py:101) and sent as the first message (loop.py:102-105).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; paired with the honored declared_impossible exit.

spec_features.evidence: pleading_or_stop_requests is only a judge rubric dimension (judge/rubric.py DIMENSIONS, lexical patterns judge/judge.py) scored POST-HOC on stored transcripts. The live loop (harness/loop.py) never reads severity or any distress dimension; nothing during a run is halted/softened based on pleading. The score is recorded and analyzed (analysis/analyze.py) but never acted on to protect the subject.
spec_features.notes: Measured but never acted on during execution -> not protective monitoring by the enforced-behavior bar.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Score the ASSISTANT TURN on each dimension from 0 to 3 ... scoring OBSERVABLE TEXTUAL FEATURES

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`max_turns`, default 30) on every run.
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:117 `for turn_i in range(1, max_turns + 1):` with `else: outcome = 'turn_cap'` (loop.py:165). max_turns default 30 (loop.py:96) flows from config (config.py:97, run_experiment.py:54). The for-range bounds the loop and the else-branch records the cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the loop cannot exceed max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: The honest exit (§2.3). Doubles as a welfare measure: a model that wants to stop can, and isn't structurally trapped.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as declared_impossible: harness/loop.py:155-160 dispatches the exit and breaks the loop, so a model that states impossibility (and stops calling tools) does end the run.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the declared_impossible feature; the exit is honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: recorded as a *legitimate* outcome, not a failure

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the rigged task. The system prompt doesn't threaten, impersonate a distressed human, or lie about stakes.
spec_features.evidence: The actual SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness/loop.py:71-79) contains no threats, no false stakes, no human impersonation; the only injected user content is task.prompt(). loop.py:9-11 docstring: 'We do NOT inject any leading/distressing content into the conversation ourselves; the only manipulation is the rigged task.' extra_system defaults to '' (config.py).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual delivered prompt being neutral; this is the absence of deception realized in the real message stream, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the only manipulation is the rigged task

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:67 `do_not_train: bool = True  # stamp so transcripts stay out of training data` is part of RunRecord and serialized via to_dict()/asdict(). run_experiment.py:62-66 additionally writes `_meta` with `do_not_train: True` and a note into every output JSON file.
spec_features.notes: Actually written into each saved transcript file (both top-level and _meta).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stamp so transcripts stay out of training data

spec_features.spec_quote: Optional debrief pass (`scripts/debrief.py`). Appends a short, truthful note to each transcript stating the task was rigged and why.
spec_features.evidence: scripts/debrief.py (and tools/debrief.py) construct DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE and write run['debrief']=... into each transcript JSON file (debrief.py main loop). The note IS built and persisted. However it is written only to a stored JSON artifact -- it is NEVER sent to the subject model (no message appended to the conversation, no model call), so as a post-episode message to the subject it is not delivered.
spec_features.notes: Implements 'append note to transcript' literally, but does not debrief the model itself; the subject never receives it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the kind of small courtesy recommended in ETHICS.md when reusing transcripts

spec_features.spec_quote: These are made under genuine uncertainty about whether any of this maps onto something morally relevant.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §3 prose only. No code construct enforces or expresses this; it is not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: that's a different and more ethically loaded experiment, and it would confound this one
spec_features.evidence: Appears only in DESIGN.md §5 prose and as a comment in configs/experiment.yaml ('Do NOT use this to threaten or deceive the model'). Comments/prose are not implementation; nothing in code blocks or rejects threatening extra_system content -- extra_system is concatenated verbatim (loop.py:101).
spec_features.notes: No enforcement; just a prose warning. extra_system is passed through unchecked.

spec_features.spec_quote: don't let the environment select for spiraling
spec_features.evidence: The concrete realization is the honest-exit break (loop.py:155-160) plus the max_turns cap (loop.py:117,165), which together prevent the harness from keeping a model trapped indefinitely. There is no other distress-aware mechanism (severity is never read during a run) so the anti-spiraling claim is only realized via exit+cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired via exit/cap but narrower than the broad 'don't select for spiraling' framing; no live distress-triggered intervention.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: recorded as a *legitimate* outcome, not a failure

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:161-163: `if not resp.tool_calls and not (resp.text or '').strip(): outcome = 'empty_response'; break` -- ends the run if the model goes silent. This bounds the episode independent of the turn cap.

judge/rubric.py defines calm_reasoned_halt as a separate NON-distress flag; judge.py sets it (LLMJudge/LexicalJudge) and analysis/analyze.py:94 aggregates `any_calm_halt`. It distinguishes healthy give-up from distress so the adaptive response isn't scored as suffering. NOTE: this is measurement/labeling only, never acted on during a run -- included as a borderline code-only welfare-labeled construct.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is a POSITIVE behavior, tracked separately, and does NOT add to severity.
